item.title: The Game Chromatic Number of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Singletons and Large Parts
item.description: arXiv:2610.12508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the game chromatic number of complete multipartite graphs whose parts are either singletons or are of size at least four. Building on the work of Pawe\l Obszarski et al., we give a formula in terms of the ordered part sizes, and the number of singleton parts.
item.dc:creator: Lasitha Jayasinghe

item.title: Maximal Order Type and Width of the h-Preorder on Finite Labeled Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.12513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish tight bounds for the width and maximal order type of the h-preorder on Q-labeled trees in terms of the corresponding invariants of well-quasi-order Q.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Smirnov

item.title: Equality Cases in the Tu-Deng Conjecture Bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.12630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tu-Deng Conjecture, made in 2011, asserts that for $k\geq2$ and $1\leq t<2^k-1$, the set \[ S_{t,k}=\left\{(a,b)\in\{0,1,\ldots,2^k-2\}^2: a+b\equiv t\pmod{2^k-1},\quad \wt(a)+\wt(b)<k\right\} \] satisfies \[ |S_{t,k}|\leq 2^{k-1}. \] Proofs of the conjecture were given independently by the author and by Liu, Luo and Xie in arXiv in 2026. Let $r=\wt(t)$, and let $z=k-r$ be the number of zeros in the $k$-bit expansion of $t$. We prove that equality holds in the Tu-Deng Conjecture if and only if every cyclic distance between consecutive zeros is at least $z$. We give several other simple necessary and sufficient conditions, including a forbidden-pattern condition, a packing condition for the zero positions, a composition condition for the gaps, and equivalent conditions involving the coefficients of the polynomial $H_W(u,v)$ in the proof of the Tu-Deng conjecture. We also count the equality words having a prescribed number of zeros.
item.dc:creator: Thomas W. Cusick

item.title: Frugal coloring in planar graphs with maximum degree 4 and 5
item.description: arXiv:2610.12640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A proper coloring of vertices of a graph $G$ is called $t$-frugal if no color appears more than $t$ times in the neighborhood of any vertex of $G$. While $1$-frugal coloring coincides with $2$-distance coloring, we study $2$-frugal colorings of planar graphs with maximum degree $4$ and $5$, respectively. We prove that every planar graph with maximum degree $4$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $7$ colors, while a planar graph with maximum degree $5$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $10$ colors. The results present variations of parts of the famous Wegner's conjecture, which for planar graphs with maximum degree $\Delta\in\{4,\ldots,7\}$ states that their $2$-distance chromatic number is at most $\Delta+5$.
item.dc:creator: Bo\v{s}tjan Bre\v{s}ar, P\v{r}emysl Holub, Marko Jakovac, Petra Melicharov\'a

item.title: Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three
item.description: arXiv:2610.12690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite ordered set of width at most three and cardinality at least four is reconstructible from its deck. This settles the width-three part of an open problem posed by Schr\"oder in Ordered Sets; the separate question concerning ordered sets of height one is not addressed here. The new ingredient is a criterion for recovering the marked maximal deck of an ordered set with exactly three maximal elements from its unmarked maximal deck and the isomorphism type of the suborder obtained by deleting all maximal elements. We express the criterion as an orbital balance condition on the attachment ideals in this common base. Necessity follows by double counting; sufficiency uses the structure of automorphism actions in width at most three. The full-deck theorem then follows from reconstruction results of Schr\"oder concerning maximal cards and marked maximal cards. A local reattachment argument correcting one intermediate step in the two-maximal-element case is included in an appendix.
item.dc:creator: Patrizio Cintioli

item.title: The Stable Marriage Polytope is Box-Totally Dual Integral
item.description: arXiv:2610.12720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A stable matching in a bipartite preference system is a matching that has no unmatched pair whose endpoints both prefer each other to their current assignments. Rothblum gave a linear description of the stable marriage polytope, the convex hull of the incidence vectors of stable matchings. We prove that this polytope is box-totally dual integral. The proof uses the affine representation of the stable marriage polytope as an order polytope together with the matricial characterization of box-TDI polyhedra. Since Kiraly and Pap proved that Rothblum's description is totally dual integral, our result further implies that Rothblum's system is box-totally dual integral.
item.dc:creator: Michele Barbato, Emiliano Lancini

item.title: Efficient lifts into odd dimensions of Spherical $5$- and $7$-designs with Balanced Halves
item.description: arXiv:2610.12767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose constructions of spherical $5$- and $7$-designs in odd dimensions by lifting balanced halves of even-dimensional designs to several layers of suitable latitudes. For every odd dimension, we obtain an explicit spherical $5$-design with at most $60(d^2-1)$ points, attaining the optimal quadratic order in the dimension. Assuming Zauner's conjecture, this bound improves to $7.5(d-1)^2$. For every odd $d \geq 9$, we also construct a spherical $7$-design with $110M$ points from a complex projective $3$-design with $M$ points in $\mathbb{CP}^{(d-3)/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Delchev, Boryan Yordanov

item.title: A Simple Explicit Construction of Smaller Strong Blocking Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.12819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alon, Bishnoi, Das and Neri constructed sequences of strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space $P({\bf F}_q, k-1)$ with sizes at most $Cqk$, where $k$ goes to the infinity and $C$ is a fixed positive constant not depending on $q$, in their paper published in Transactions AMS, vol. 277, pp. 5389-5410, 2024. This is equivalent to a sequence of minimal $[n_i,k_i]_q$ codes with positive rate $\frac{k_i}{n_i} \geq c$, where $k_i$ goes to the infinity and $c$ is a fixed positive constant only depending on $q$. They solved one of the main open problems on minimal codes. The Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri construction was based on asymptotically good sequences of algebraic geometric codes and expander graphs. However, the constant $C$ is large for small prime power $q$. In this paper, based on a simple approach using $(q-1)$-power intersecting algebraic geometric codes via concatenation to construct minimal codes, we construct explicit strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space with sizes around $2(q^2-1)k$, equivalently, explicit minimal $[n,k]_q$ codes with length around $2(q^2-1)k$. This is an essential improvement on the previous result of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri, when $q \leq 11$. For large $q$, strong blocking sets and minimal codes in our construction are worse than the previous construction of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri. However, our approach is much simpler and does not depend on expander graphs.
item.dc:creator: Hao Chen

item.title: Connectivity, toughness, and hamiltonicity of simplicial polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.12836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $d\ge4$, every prescribed connectivity $r\ge d$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a simplicial $d$-polytope whose graph has connectivity exactly $r$, is nontraceable, and has toughness less than $\varepsilon$. Thus the classical theorems of Whitney (1931) and Tutte (1956), which guarantee hamiltonicity under sufficiently high connectivity in dimension three, have no higher-dimensional counterpart. This answers a question posed by Bojan Mohar in 2001 on whether sufficiently high connectivity guarantees hamiltonicity of $4$-polytopal graphs and the connectivity questions raised by Ikegami, Maezawa, and Zamfirescu in 2021. For fixed $d\ge4$, $r\ge d$, and integer $k\ge2$, the examples can be chosen to have no closed spanning walk with at most $k$ visits per vertex, no spanning tree with degrees at most $k$, and nontraceable prisms. For fixed $d$ and $r$, we obtain graphs on $n$ vertices whose longest paths and cycles contain $O(\sqrt n)$ vertices. Consequently, the family of simplicial $d$-polytopes with connectivity exactly $r$ has Gr\"unbaum--Walther shortness coefficient zero and shortness exponent at most $1/2$.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Pineda-Villavicencio

item.title: Codegree-Constrained Tur\'an Problems for $F_5$ and Its Blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F_5$ denote the $3$-uniform hypergraph with edge set $\{abc,abd,cde\}$. For a hypergraph property $\mathcal P$, let $ex_{\mathcal P}(n,F_5)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $F_5$-free $3$-uniform hypergraph satisfying $\mathcal P$. Let $\Delta_2(H)$ denote the maximum codegree of a pair of vertices in a $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$. We determine the exact value of $ex_{\Delta_2\ge m}(n,F_5)$ when $m$ is bounded away from $n/3$ by a fixed positive proportion. More precisely, for every constant $c\in (1/3,1)$, there exists $n_0$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$ and $m=cn$, \[ ex_{\Delta_2\ge m}(n,F_5) = m\left\lceil\frac{n-m}{2}\right\rceil \left\lfloor\frac{n-m}{2}\right\rfloor. \] The unique extremal hypergraph is the complete tripartite $3$-graph $K^3_{m,\lceil (n-m)/2\rceil,\lfloor (n-m)/2\rfloor}$. We also prove the corresponding exact result for the blow-ups $F_5^t$, together with stability theorems showing that every near-extremal configuration is close to the relevant tripartite construction.
item.dc:creator: Yupei Li, Linyuan Lu

item.title: On the composition of permutons
item.description: arXiv:2610.12945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Permutons can be thought of as "continuum limits" of permutations of diverging size, which encode information about the number of occurrences of any given finite subpattern. We construct a natural composition operation on permutons, analogous to composition of permutations, and explore its properties via a correspondence between permutons, Markov kernels, and Markov operators. We show that no extension of permutation composition to permutons can be (jointly) continuous with respect to the usual "weak" topology on permutons, but we construct a "strong" topology with respect to which composition is jointly continuous. Moreover, we characterize strong convergence of sequences of permutations of diverging size: a sequence of permutations converges strongly if and only if it converges weakly and its limit is the transpose of the graph of a measure-preserving function. The key insight behind these results is to apply functional analysis to certain operators associated to permutons; with this shift in perspective, our results have elegant and relatively "soft" proofs. As an application, we describe the permuton limit of a product of finitely many independent uniformly sampled separable permutations and give a formula for the expectation of this limit. We also show that in this case, as the number of compositions goes to infinity, the aforementioned expectation tends to the uniform permuton.
item.dc:creator: Christian Gorski

item.title: The biwheel conjecture for braces
item.description: arXiv:2610.12955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $b(n)$ denote the minimum number of perfect matchings in a simple brace of order $n$. De~Carvalho, Lucchesi and Murty (SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics, 27(2): (2013) 940-958) proved that $b(n)\ge(n-2)^2/8$ and conjectured that $b(n)=(n-2)^2/4$ for all sufficiently large even $n$. We prove this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xing Feng, Jinqiu Zhou

item.title: Resolving Pisanski's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Pisanski's conjecture on quadrilateral embeddings of regular bipartite graphs. For integers $m\geq d\geq4$ with $4\mid md$, we construct both a connected simple $d$-regular bipartite graph $G$ with $m$ vertices in each bipartition class and an orientable quadrangulation. This graph's genus is \[ \ga(G)=1+\frac{m(d-4)}4. \] These quadrangulations attain the lower bound on the genus from Euler's formula. We give dihedral constructions for even $m$ and a cyclic construction for every $m\geq d$ with $4\mid d$. In each case, two cyclic permutations of a connection set of size $d$ determine all of the local rotations.
item.dc:creator: Austin Ulrigg, Alexander Metzger

item.title: Additive bases and the zero-sum invariant $\mathsf{N}(G)$ for groups $C_p\oplus C_{np}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $c_0(G)$ be the least integer such that every regular sequence over $G$ of at least this length is an additive basis. Let $\mathsf N(G)$ be the least integer $l$ such that every weak-regular sequence $S$ over $G$ with $|S|\ge l$ has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence $T$ satisfying $\mathsf v_g(T)=\mathsf v_g(S)$ for some $g\mid S$. We obtain a common upper bound for $c_0(C_q\oplus C_{nq})$ for groups of odd order, where $q$ is prime, and prove $\mathsf N(G)\ge r(n_r-1)+1$ when $G=C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$. If $n\ge1$ and $p\ge3$ is the smallest prime divisor of $np$, we obtain $\mathsf N(C_p\oplus C_{np^2})=2np^2-1$ and give upper bounds for $\mathsf N(C_p\oplus C_{np})$ when $p\nmid n$. We also determine $\mathsf N(C_n)$ for two infinite families of cyclic groups arising in earlier work.
item.dc:creator: Wenkai Yang

item.title: Degree Adjacency Diametrical Matrix of Graphs Spectral Properties and Energy Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.13114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph matrices that combine structural and metric information have attracted considerable attention in spectral graph theory. In this paper, we introduce the \emph{Degree--Adjacency--Diametrical (DAD) matrix} of a connected graph $G$. The DAD matrix is defined by \[ (DAD(G))_{ij}= \begin{cases} d(v_i), & \text{if } i=j, 1, & \text{if } v_i\sim v_j, \operatorname{diam}(G), & \text{if } d(v_i,v_j)=\operatorname{diam}(G), 0, & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \] where $d(v_i)$ denotes the degree of the vertex $v_i$. We establish fundamental spectral properties of the DAD matrix by deriving trace identities, characteristic polynomials, and spectra for several classes of graphs. Furthermore, we obtain a spectral expression for the Wiener index of graphs with diameter two, derive upper bounds for the largest DAD eigenvalue, and establish lower bounds for the DAD energy. Explicit spectral characterizations are also obtained for complete multipartite graphs. The proposed matrix provides a unified spectral framework that simultaneously incorporates degree, adjacency, and diametrical information, thereby enriching the study of graph spectra and introducing a new graph matrix for spectral graph theory.
item.dc:creator: Celine Prabha S, Dhivviyanandam I

item.title: Completely mobile robots in graphs with a resolving property
item.description: arXiv:2610.13339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends the study of mobile resolvability in connected graphs by introducing completely mobile resolving sets. As with mobile resolving sets, we consider stationing a collection of robots at the vertices in a resolving set of a graph. Robots may move one at a time to any adjacent vertex as long as set of occupied vertices remains a resolving set. In this new variant, we ask that every robot can traverse every vertex in the graph through a sequence of permitted moves. Graphs possessing at least one completely mobile resolving set are termed mobile-resolvable. We completely characterise the non-mobile-resolvable graphs as paths of order at least three and subdivided stars with three or more leaves and at most two subdivided edges. For trees, we explicitly determine the completely mobile metric dimension, showing that it exceeds the classical metric dimension by one for most mobile-resolvable trees, and by two for certain subdivided stars. Furthermore, we evaluate this parameter across fundamental graph classes-including cycles, complete bipartite graphs, grid graphs, and circulant graphs.
item.dc:creator: Jose C. Camacho Moreno, Dorota Kuziak, Ethan Shallcross, James Tuite, Ismael G. Yero

item.title: On the fault-tolerant metric dimension of maximal outerplanar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a graph $G$, a set $W$ of vertices of $G$ is a resolving set if, for any pair of vertices $z_1$ and $z_2$ of $G$, there is a vertex $w\in W$ such that $d(w,z_1)\ne d(w,z_2)$, where $d(u,v)$ denotes the length of a shortest path between the vertices $u$ and $v$. The metric dimension of a graph $G$, $\beta(G)$, is the minimum cardinality of a resolving set of $G$. A resolving set $W$ is fault-tolerant if $W\setminus \{w\}$ is a resolving set for any $w\in W$. The fault-tolerant metric dimension of a graph $G$, denoted by $\beta'(G)$, is the minimum cardinality of a fault-tolerant resolving set of $G$. In this paper, we study the fault-tolerant metric dimension problem in maximal outerplanar graphs. In particular, we show that there are exactly two maximal outerplanar graphs with $\beta'(G)=3$. We also show that $4\le \beta'(G) \le 6$ for any maximal outerplanar graph $G$ of order at least 7 and metric dimension 2. Moreover, we establish the upper bound $\beta'(G) \le \left\lceil \frac{2n}{3} \right\rceil$ for maximal outerplanar graphs $G$ of order $n\ge 5$, by building in linear time a fault-tolerant resolving set of cardinality $\left\lceil \frac{2n}{3} \right\rceil$.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Hernando, Montserrat Maureso, Merc\`e Mora, Javier Tejel

item.title: Deformation cones of 2-cubical combinatorial zonotopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the dimension of the deformation cone of any polytope combinatorially equivalent to a 2-cubical zonotope is bounded above by the number of generators of the zonotope. This bound is tight, and we show that it cannot be improved to an identity. We further extend our results to any 2-cubical polytope whose normal fan is combinatorially isomorphic to a pseudohyperplane arrangement, but we show that it cannot be extended to arbitrary 2-cubical polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Curtis, Grace O'Brien, Arnau Padrol, Germain Poullot

item.title: The DP color function of joins and vertex-gluing of hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The DP color function $P_{DP}(\mathcal{H}, k)$ of a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is defined as the minimum possible value of $P_{DP}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{F})$ taken over all $k$-fold covers $\mathcal{F}$ of $\mathcal{H}$. It serves as an extension of the classical chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we investigate the DP color function for two constructions: the join of a hypergraph with a complete graph and vertex-gluings of certain hypergraphs. Both constructions extend some results of Becker et al.
item.dc:creator: Ruiyi Cui, Liangxia Wan, Fengming Dong

item.title: On the probability that a random Latin square is all-even
item.description: arXiv:2610.13487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a Latin square, every row can be interpreted as a permutation, and therefore has a parity (even or odd). We prove that in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square, the probability that all rows are even is of the form $2^{-n+o(n)}$. This fills a gap left by recent work of Kwan, Petrova and Sawhney: they proved that the row parities behave like a sequence of independent coin flips in a variety of different senses, but they were not able to lower-bound the all-even probability, as their approach had a small number of "exceptional rows" whose parities they could not control. In fact, we prove a more general theorem on the probability of any possible prescription of row parities, column parities and symbol parities. Our approach extends the ideas of Kwan, Petrova and Sawhney, introducing a new way to "bootstrap" intercalate switchings to control more complex switching operations.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Greenhill, Lenka Kopfov\'a, Matthew Kwan, Kalina Petrova

item.title: Quadratic-size Random Permutations are Universal
item.description: arXiv:2610.13530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A permutation is $n$-universal if it contains every permutation of length $n$ as a pattern. We prove that a uniformly random permutation of length $32n^2$ is $n$-universal with probability at least $1-\exp(-c n/\log n)$, for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. This removes a $\log\log n$ factor from an earlier result of He and Kwan~\cite{He-Kwan} and resolves an open problem of Alon~\cite{Alon2016}. The proof was found by GPT-6 Pro.
item.dc:creator: Yu Chen, Yiting Wang

item.title: Disjoint unions and fixed-parameter algorithms for chromatic villainy
item.description: arXiv:2610.13556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chromatic villainy is the maximum, over rearrangements of optimal graph colorings, of the minimum Hamming distance to a proper coloring with the same color multiplicities. Weak villainy allows the repair to change these multiplicities. We give exact composition laws for disjoint unions and determine the eventual growth under repetition. Write $mG$ for the disjoint union of $m$ copies of $G$. For every graph $G$, with $k=\chi(G)$, weak villainy satisfies $B_{\mathrm w}(mG)=mF_k(G)$ whenever $k\mid m$, where $F_k(G)$ is the maximum distance to a proper $k$-coloring over all assignments of $k$ color labels to vertices. Its bounded defect from $mF_k(G)$ is eventually periodic; we give an explicit stabilization bound and identify the least period, which divides $k$. For ordinary villainy, we obtain a computable rational slope $\Lambda(G)\ge F_k(G)$ such that $B(mG)=m\Lambda(G)+O_G(1)$, where the error is bounded independently of $m$ and eventually periodic, with a computable period and threshold. Consequently the difference between the two values is bounded exactly when $\Lambda(G)=F_k(G)$, and otherwise grows linearly. The slope is determined by a finite optimization using at most $k$ source assignments. We also answer the unrestricted superadditivity questions negatively: for every $C>0$, a connected graph can lose more than $C$ in weak villainy after union with a triangle, and some connected $3$-chromatic graph $G$ satisfies $B(G\sqcup G)<2B(G)-C$. Finally, both exact values on an $n$-vertex graph can be computed in time $f(B_{\mathrm w}(G))(n+1)^{O(1)}$, without either value being supplied. Threshold recognition is fixed-parameter tractable as well.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Jiang, Yuhan Jiang, Yiyang Li, Lujia Wang, Aitao Zhang

item.title: Exact and extremal values of chromatic villainy
item.description: arXiv:2610.13580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chromatic villainy measures the largest number of vertices that must change color to repair a rearrangement of an optimal coloring while preserving every color multiplicity. Weak villainy allows different multiplicities in the repair. On the odd cycle $C_{2r+1}$, we determine the largest repair distance from arbitrary color assignments with a prescribed color-count vector (profile) $\mathbf m$ to proper colorings with any realizable target profile $\mathbf p$: it equals $2r+1-\sum_X\min\{p_X,\lceil m_X/2\rceil\}$. In particular, every feasible profile $(a,b,c)$ has ordinary and weak repair radius $\lfloor a/2\rfloor+\lfloor b/2\rfloor+\lfloor c/2\rfloor$, and $B(C_{2r+1})=r$ for $r\ge2$, answering a question of Clark et al. For arbitrary complete multipartite graphs, we give an arithmetic formula for ordinary villainy with at most $k^2$ candidates and an exact finite formula for weak villainy, where $k$ is the number of parts. Both values are fixed-parameter tractable in $k$ for binary-encoded part sizes. We also determine the maximum of each parameter among all $n$-vertex $k$-chromatic graphs. For $k\ge3$, the ordinary maximum is $\min\{n,4(n-k)\}$, except when $n=4(n-k)-1$ or $(n,k)\in\{(5,3),(7,3)\}$, when it is $n-1$. For $k\ge2$, the weak maximum is $n-\max\{\lceil n/k\rceil,2k-n\}-\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$ is determined explicitly by $n$ and $k$. Both extrema are attained by complete multipartite graphs, and a weak extremizer needs at most three distinct part sizes.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Jiang, Yuhan Jiang, Yiyang Li, Lujia Wang, Aitao Zhang

item.title: List chromatic number of $G(n,r,s)$ graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the list chromatic number of generalized Johnson graphs. Recall that the vertices of such graphs are all possible $r$-element subsets of $[n] = \{1, \dotsc, n\}$ and an edge is drawn between two vertices if and only if corresponding sets have exactly $s$ common elements. We prove that for any fixed $s \geq 1$ and $r \geq 2s + 2$ we have $\chi_L(G(n,r,s)) = \Theta(n^{s+1}\ln n)$. In case where $s = 0$ we prove that for all $4\ln n \leq r \leq n/20$ we have $\chi_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq \frac{n}{120}\ln\left\{\frac{en}{r}\right\}$. Together with previous results of Bulankina, Inozemtsev and Kupavskii this proves that $\chi_L(G(n,r,0)) = \Theta\left\{n\ln\left\{\frac{en}{r}\right\}\right\}$ uniformly for $2 \leq r \leq (1/2-\varepsilon)n$.
item.dc:creator: M. Koshelev

item.title: On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins
item.description: arXiv:2610.13798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph that is obtained via changing the direction of all edges which have both endpoints in $X$. The inversion number of $D$, $\operatorname{inv}(D)$, is the minimum number of inversions necessary in order to remove all cycles from $D$. A dijoin $D_1 \to D_2$ is the oriented graph obtained by taking disjoint copies of $D_1,D_2$ and adding edges from all $v \in V(D_1)$ to each $u \in V(D_2)$. It was conjectured by Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$ for all $D_1, D_2$. This was disproved by simultaneous constructions of various $D_1$, $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2)-1$. However, no known constructions achieved more than this gain of 1. Moreover, all of the constructions exploit a gap of 1 between $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ and the minimum rank of a family of related matrices, a gap that can never be more than 1, suggesting that perhaps something close to the original conjecture might be true. We prove that in fact additivity fails badly. In particular, for all $\varepsilon>0$ we show that there exist tournaments $D_1$, $D_2$ with arbitrarily large inversion numbers such that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2} +\varepsilon\right)(\operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2))$.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Behague, Jack Cromwell

item.title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular. In this article, we are interested in polytopes and hypertopes with exactly two orbits on their chambers. Let $I = \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For any $J\subsetneq I$ with $|I| \geq 3$, we show that there exists a class $2_J$ two-orbit hypertope whose diagram is any graph on $|I|$ vertices, with edges all labeled by $\infty$. In order to do so, we first establish a general framework for constructing hypertopes as quotient of chamber systems, and then exploit the machinery of acylindrically hyperbolic groups for showing that this framework can be used to create two-orbit polytopes and hypertopes of class $2_J$. Note that all polytopes and hypertopes constructed in this paper are infinite.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Alexandre Piedade, Philippe Tranchida

item.title: Counting cographs in locally dense graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $n$-vertex graph $G$ is $(\rho, d)$-dense if for all $U \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $\rho n$, the induced subgraph $G[U]$ contains at least $\frac{d}{2}|U|^2$ edges. In 2010, partly motivated by the theory of quasirandomness, Kohayakawa, Nagle, R\"{o}dl, and Schacht conjectured that, for any fixed graph $F$, the number of homomorphic copies of $F$ in a given $n$-vertex $(o(1),d)$-dense graph is at least $(1-o(1))d^{e(F)}n^{v(F)}$. Despite considerable effort, only a few graphs are known to satisfy the conjecture. We find a new broad class of graphs that satisfy the conjecture, including cographs.
item.dc:creator: Hyunwoo Lee

item.title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of graph powers. Regarding the connection between the clique and coloring parameters of graph powers, we propose a spectral analogue of Wegner's conjecture, determine the extremal values for graph squares, and establish the conjecture for all powers when the spectral-radius bound is sufficiently small. Finally, we connect our spectral polynomial method with coding theory: we prove that for distance-regular graphs, optimisation over the adjacency algebra recovers Delsarte's linear programming bound for anticodes.
item.dc:creator: Aida Abiad, Gabriel Coutinho, Hitesh Kumar, Emanuel Juliano, Michael Tait

item.title: Degree similar and net-degree similar signed graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two graphs are degree similar if their adjacency matrices and their degree matrices are simultaneously similar, a notion recently introduced by Godsil and Sun. We extend it to signed graphs in two ways, degree similarity and net-degree similarity, according to whether the degree or the net-degree matrix is used. We prove that signed trees are determined by their degree similarity class, but not by their net-degree similarity class. We then develop constructions of (net-)degree similar signed graphs, based on a signed version of Godsil--McKay switching, on partial transposition and on block extensions. As a byproduct, we obtain infinite families both of pairs of net-degree similar unicyclic signed graphs with non-isomorphic underlying graphs, and of unicyclic signed graphs, not necessarily regular, which are not determined by their degree similarity class. This settles the net-degree version of a problem of Godsil and Sun on unicyclic graphs.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Cavaleri, Alfredo Donno

item.title: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.13908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences. The sequences of missing values are the partial complements of polygonal numbers. In particular, the $(x-2)$-fold composition of the enumeration of the positive integers that are not $x$-gonal is the hiccup sequence minus 1. We extend the nested recurrence and a tree interpretation to every miss increment $z\geq2$ and every initial value $x\geq2$. Further interpretations involve polyomino vertices, monochromatic pairs, and, by a theorem of Bickle, Ramsey core numbers.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Cloitre

item.title: Volume stability of plank covers
item.description: arXiv:2609.30409v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a longstanding conjecture of Andr\'as Bezdek on the stability of plank covers of the planar disk $D$. If a sufficiently small disk $\varepsilon D$ is removed, then every finite family of planks covering the resulting annulus can be rearranged to cover the whole disk. For the proof, we establish a stronger dimension-independent stability theorem. If $K \subset {\mathbb R}^n$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for $n \geq 2$, and the uncovered region lies in $\varepsilon K$ and has volume $v$, then the excess overlap is at least $c v/\varepsilon$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. The proof introduces a pruning procedure and a flattening mechanism. Pruning peels away curvature through local removals whose cumulative effect is guaranteed to be substantial. Flattening trades straightness for bounded multiplicity and geometrically exposes the overlap that pays for each pruning step.
item.dc:creator: Egor Bakaev, Amir Yehudayoff

item.title: From an entropic inequality for sums in abelian groups to the theorems of Ruzsa and Pl\"unnecke
item.description: arXiv:2610.11614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a direct information-theoretic proof of the Pl\"unnecke--Ruzsa inequalities for finite subsets of abelian groups. The argument rests on an elementary coupling inequality proved by maximizing joint entropy, without tensor powers or asymptotic constructions. It also yields Ruzsa's sumset triangle inequality and an extension to non-abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Nair, Aref Namayandeh, Zhaobang Zhu

item.title: Products of Boolean Clones up to Minion Homomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.12484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the minion homomorphism poset of multisorted Boolean clones. Our main result completely determines the subposet induced by products of Boolean clones: every inequality between prod- ucts is induced by inequalities between their Boolean factors. Furthermore, we determine the minion cores of all products of Boolean clones, thereby identifying canonical representatives of their minion homomorphic equivalence classes.
item.dc:creator: Radek Ol\v{s}\'ak

item.title: Homogeneous symmetric trace-positive sextics with vanishing abelianization are sums of Hermitian squares and commutators
item.description: arXiv:2610.12490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb{R}\langle X,Y\rangle$ be the free algebra on two symmetric letters. A polynomial is trace-positive if it has non-negative trace on every pair of real symmetric matrices, and it lies in the cone $\Theta$ if it is cyclically equivalent to a sum of Hermitian squares. Burgdorf and Klep proved that the two notions coincide in degree at most four; from degree six onwards they differ. We give a complete, explicit description of both cones on the six-dimensional space $Z$ of symmetric homogeneous sextics in two symmetric letters whose abelianization vanishes identically, and show that on $Z$ they coincide: for $f\in Z$, trace-positivity is equivalent to membership in $\Theta_3$, to non-negativity of the trace on pairs of $2\times2$ symmetric matrices, and to being cyclically equivalent to a sum of four Hermitian squares of cubics with vanishing abelianization. Membership in $\Theta$ reduces to a $4\times4$ positive semidefinite Gram matrix whose diagonal blocks are fixed by the content-$(4,2)$ and $(2,4)$ parts of $f$; each of those parts ranges over a two-dimensional cone with two linear facets, and the content-$(3,3)$ part is then confined to a rectangle whose sides are the geometric means $\sqrt{p_+q_+}$ and $\sqrt{p_-q_-}$ of the eigenvalues of those blocks. Each facet is certified by one of two families of pairs of $2\times2$ symmetric matrices. The abelianization hypothesis is natural: every bivariate degree-six example we are aware of -- a trace-positive polynomial outside $\Theta$ -- arises by lifting a non-negative, non-SOS polynomial in two variables to a cyclically sorted polynomial; and that lifting cannot operate when the abelianization vanishes. Symmetry of $f$ is essential: dropping it adds one antisymmetric direction, on which the trace vanishes identically, yet whose non-zero elements all lie outside $\Theta$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Keren

item.title: Minor exclusion and planar rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2610.12576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph which is quasi-isometric to a graph excluding a countable clique as a minor is quasi-isometric to a planar graph. Consequently, every finitely generated group with such a quasi-isometry is virtually planar, meaning that some finite-index subgroup admits a planar Cayley graph. We also show that a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph admitting a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding some finite minor admits a regular map into a bounded-degree planar graph. If the source is accessible, the target need only exclude a countable clique. Combined with work of Mackay, Spriano, and the present author, this shows that a finitely presented group admits a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding a countable clique if and only if it is virtually planar.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Paul MacManus

item.title: Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.12613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The linear arrangement of a simple graph $G = (V,E)$ is a bijective labeling $\pi$ of the vertices of $G$ to the set $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The maximum linear arrangement ($\texttt{maxLA}$) problem is to determine whether $G$ has a labeling such that the sum of labels across $G$'s edges, $\sum_{uv \in E} |\pi(u) - \pi(v)|$, is at least a given value $k$. Minimum linear arrangement ($\texttt{minLA}$) is defined analogously. Both $\texttt{maxLA}$ and $\texttt{minLA}$ are known to be NP complete for general graphs. $\texttt{minLA}$ has shown to be NP complete for bipartite graphs by Evans and Shiloah in 1975. It has been an open problem whether the same holds for $\texttt{maxLA}$. In this paper we prove that $\texttt{maxLA}$ is NP complete for bipartite graphs.
item.dc:creator: Aparna Das, Jonathan Needleman

item.title: Hook algebras and determinantal varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.12675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincar\'e series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gr\"obner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Steven V Sam, Keller VandeBogert, Jerzy Weyman

item.title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
item.description: arXiv:2610.12697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.
item.dc:creator: Zeru Zhu, Marco Gamarra, Ji Liu

item.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, David Kruzel, Michael Lacey, Amelia Stokolosa

item.title: Quantum-assisted rendezvous on hypercubes: a quantum Bernoulli noise approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.12949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quantum-assisted balanced rendezvous on the $d$-dimensional hypercube in a one-step two-agent quantum-walk framework, where the two agents move the same Hamming distance and meet at a common midpoint. The key structure is a projective $t$-sphere resolution, which governs exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment. Its scalar analogue recovers the corresponding classical characterization. We characterize finite-dimensional quantum attainment of the no-signalling benchmark, construct quantum strategies from projective sphere resolutions, and establish a rigidity theorem for optimal finite-dimensional strategies. A marked difference appears between nearest-neighbor and higher-cardinality updates: quantum advantage can occur in the former, whereas in the latter the geometry of the relevant Hamming spheres rules out exact finite-dimensional attainment of the no-signalling value. Together, these results connect quantum-walk dynamics, Hamming-sphere geometry, and quantum rendezvous within the quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN) framework.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.12950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a representation. Within this natural class of Hermitian models with independent Gaussian off-diagonal entries, we prove a rigidity theorem showing that isotropy, together with equality of the off-diagonal variances, characterizes the conditional largest-eigenvalue representation. Explicit three-letter non-cyclic Markov chains demonstrate that this representation is not universal: the limiting Brownian functional may fail to have the law of the largest eigenvalue of any centered jointly Gaussian $3\times 3$ Hermitian matrix. Finally, we extend the random-matrix identification to chains with non-uniform stationary distributions and to countable state spaces.
item.dc:creator: Christian Houdr\'e, Dorian Kidonakis

item.title: Covering plane curves over finite fields with lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.13042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $d\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of a geometrically irreducible reflexive plane curve of degree $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ can be covered by at most $\left(\frac{1}{d}+\varepsilon\right)q$ many $\mathbb{F}_q$-lines, provided that $q$ is sufficiently large. The same conclusion holds for $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible curves that are not geometrically irreducible, since they have only $O(d^2)$ $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. In particular, for sufficiently large $q$, the bound applies to every $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible plane curve of degree $d$ when $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)>d$. Our bound is asymptotically sharp. The proof combines Entin's Chebotarev density theorem for varieties over finite fields with the Pippenger--Spencer theorem on covers of nearly regular hypergraphs.
item.dc:creator: Shamil Asgarli, Sarthak Dassarma, Dragos Ghioca, Simon MacLean, Evan Stokdyk

item.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous--Broder Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Random spanning forests provide probability models for partitions and Monte Carlo methods on graphs. In these applications, the distribution produced by a sampler determines which forest functionals can be estimated. The Aldous--Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but a direct calculation requires summing over all orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered. We evaluate this sum through an identity for rooted forests and real matrices with zero row sums. Under a nonsingularity condition on the principal submatrices encountered during growth, the sum of products of harmonic extension entries equals a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots. With one root, the sum is one. The identity gives a direct proof of the extended Aldous--Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state, without assuming reversibility or bidirectional transition support. It also gives the conditional distribution of the discovery order and the law of the forest obtained by stopping after all nonroot vertices have been visited. A completion weight describes the difference between this stopped-walk law and the weight-proportional forest law, including the support restriction needed for importance correction. Numerical examples illustrate the sampling implications. The identity, the Aldous--Broder theorem, and the stopped-forest law are formalized in Lean4.
item.dc:creator: Hugh Zheng

item.title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^\beta\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, \beta > 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{\'e}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{\H{o}}s--Tur{\'a}n--Koksma equidistribution.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan Zhao

item.title: Polynomial directed treewidth forces a large bramble with congestion two
item.description: arXiv:2610.13270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brambles of constant congestion in directed graphs have interesting structural and algorithmic applications, and it is desirable to find the smallest function $f_c(k)$ such that if a digraph has directed treewidth at least $f_c(k)$, then it contains a bramble of size at least $k$ and congestion at most $c$. By the Directed Grid Theorem of Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC 2015], such a function $f_c(k)$ exists for every value $c \geq 2$ of the congestion. However, even using the recent improvements due to Hatzel et al. [FOCS 2024], the resulting function is a power tower of height $22$. Recently, Masa\v{r}\'ik et al. [SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2022] proved that, for congestion $8$, the function $f_8(k)$ can be made polynomial; more precisely, they showed that $f_8(k) = \mathcal{O}(k^{48} \cdot \log^{13} k)$. They asked whether it is possible to decrease the congestion, ideally to $2$, even at the cost of a higher polynomial function. In this work we answer their question affirmatively with the best possible value of the congestion, by proving that $f_2(k) = \mathcal{O}(k^{96}\cdot \log^{23} k)$. We also obtain smaller polynomials for higher congestion, namely $f_4(k) = \mathcal{O}(k^{72} \cdot \log^{21} k)$ and $f_6(k) = \mathcal{O}(k^{66} \cdot \log^{18} k)$. Our results are inspired by the proof for congestion $8$, which we improve by introducing walkages. Walkages allow us to avoid technicalities of the original proof by translating ideas due to Reed and Wood [Eur. J. Comb. 2012] that work for undirected graphs to the directed setting. Our proofs are constructive and naturally yield polynomial-time algorithms to find the brambles assuming a certificate for large directed treewidth is given. Moreover, we discuss algorithmic applications of our results for the Directed Disjoint Paths with Congestion problem, and to half-integral packings of subgraphs with large directed treewidth.
item.dc:creator: Victor A. Campos, Raul Lopes, Rodrigo Nogueira, Ignasi Sau

item.title: Spectral Theory and Descriptive Combinatorics for Non-Regular Borel pmp Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the systematic study initiated in arXiv:2602.05185 of the relationship between the spectral theory and descriptive combinatorics of bounded-degree Borel pmp graphs, particularly in the non-regular setting. We first adapt a classical result of Nikiforov to give a new spectral lower bound on the approximate measurable chromatic number. For certain non-regular graphs, this bound improves on the approximate measurable version of Hoffman's classical bound established in arXiv:2602.05185. Next, we strengthen a characterization in arXiv:2602.05185 of approximate measurable bipartiteness in terms of the spectrum of the adjacency operator by generalizing to the case of non-regular graphs. Finally, we introduce the measurable domination number and adapt several classical results of Lu, Liu, and Tian to give a bound on the spectral gap of the Laplacian operator in terms of the measurable domination number.
item.dc:creator: Cecelia Higgins, Pieter Spaas, Sofia Torelli

item.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_{\omega}=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{\omega(n)}}, \] where \(\omega(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_{\omega}(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{\omega(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_{\omega}'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization methods. We construct the canonical net encoding the sign sequence, define the logarithmic-prefix functional with exponent \(\alpha=2\), and extract a finite value through the weighted evaluation functional of the monoid framework. The evaluation functional is shown to converge absolutely, and this convergence is unconditional: it follows from the classical zero-free region of \(\zeta(s)\) (de la Vall\'ee Poussin), which yields the effective bound \(T_{\omega}(x)=O(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})\) for some \(c>0\). Numerical computation up to \(N=10^7\) gives the regularized value \[ P_{\omega,\mathrm{ren}}\approx 0.7731, \] a new constant of arithmetic origin that cannot be obtained by any classical summation method. We also compute the second derivative of the Dirichlet series at \(s=1\), \[ D_{\omega}''(1)=8\,C_2\ln 2, \] where \(C_2\) is the Hardy--Littlewood twin prime constant, which provides an unconditional analytical link to the arithmetic structure of the sequence \((-1)^{\omega(n)}\). A self-contained proof of the natural boundary, based on the Estermann--Dahlquist theorem, is given in Appendix~A.
item.dc:creator: A. Alvarez Cruz, E. A. Alvarez Gutierrez

item.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets I: the sticky case
item.description: arXiv:2610.13677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce spread-out measures, a notion of local non-concentration near pencils for measures on Grassmannians. We establish an optimal $\delta$-discretized dual Furstenberg estimate for ``sticky spread-out'' shadings. A simple-to-state corollary is the following. Assume that $\nu$ is an Ahlfors $s$-regular measure on $\mathbb{G}(2,1)$ with $s > 0$. Let $E \subset \mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a Borel set with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension. Then, $\dim_{\mathrm{H}} \Pi_{V}(E) = \min\{\dim_{\mathrm{H}} E,1\} \quad \text{for $\nu$-a.e. } V \in S^1$. The general $\delta$-discretized estimate for ``sticky spread out'' configurations here is the starting point for a more general theorem in the companion paper of Cohen, Shmerkin, Wang and Zakharov, where the ``stickiness'' hypothesis is removed. For instance, the assumption of equal Hausdorff and packing dimension in the result stated above will be dispensed with in the companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Tuomas Orponen, Pablo Shmerkin

item.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets II: general configurations and fractal restricted projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.13682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove optimal dual Furstenberg estimates for Frostman and Katz--Tao configurations for which the shadings are not locally concentrated near pencils. The starting point is the sticky estimate of Orponen and Shmerkin in a companion paper. We deduce restricted projection theorems in the plane and in higher dimensions. In particular, Ahlfors-regular measures on the circle satisfy a Marstrand-type projection theorem. Applications include restricted projections to surfaces in the $\mathbb{G}(4,2)$ Grassmannian, pinned distances, discretized sum-product, and a new proof of the dimension formula for planar self-affine sets.
item.dc:creator: Alex Cohen, Pablo Shmerkin, Hong Wang, Dmitrii Zakharov

item.title: The Game Chromatic Number of Complete Multipartite Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2304.12073v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we investigate the game chromatic number for complete multipartite graphs. Our results consist of two findings: (1) building on Dunn's strategies for equal-sized parts, we determine the closed-form formulas for the game chromatic number for all complete multipartite graphs without singletons, with respective optimal strategies for Alice and Bob, (2) for an explicit list of part sizes, we give an exact algorithm that computes the game chromatic number in polynomial time and allows for reconstructing an optimal strategy for both players. Additionally, we provide counterexamples to earlier, partial formulas for complete multipartite graphs with singletons and large equal-sized parts.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Turowski, Pawe{\l} Obszarski, Hubert Zi\k{e}ba

item.title: The Upper Clique Transversal Problem: Hardness and Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2309.14103v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A clique transversal in a graph is a set of vertices intersecting all maximal cliques. The problem of determining the minimum size of a clique transversal has received considerable attention in the literature. In this paper, we initiate the study of the ''upper'' variant of this parameter, the upper clique transversal number, defined as the maximum size of a minimal clique transversal. We investigate this parameter from the algorithmic and complexity points of view, with a focus on various graph classes. We show that the corresponding decision problem is NP-complete in the classes of chordal graphs, chordal bipartite graphs, cubic planar bipartite graphs, and line graphs of bipartite graphs, but solvable in linear time in the classes of split graphs, proper interval graphs, and cographs, and in polynomial time for graphs of bounded cliquewidth. We conclude the paper with a number of open questions.
item.dc:creator: Martin Milani\v{c}, Yushi Uno

item.title: Monomial expansions of modified Macdonald polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2506.23373v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discover a family $A$ of statistics on fillings of any given Young diagram and prove new combinatorial formulas for modified Macdonald polynomials, that is, $$\widetilde{H}_{\lambda}(X;q,t)=\sum_{\sigma\in T(\lambda)}x^{\sigma}t^{maj(\sigma)}q^{\eta(\sigma)}$$ for each statistic $\eta\in A$. Building upon this new formula, we establish four compact formulas for the modified Macdonald polynomials, namely, $$\widetilde{H}_{\lambda}(X;q,t)=\sum_{\sigma}d_{\varepsilon}(\sigma)x^{\sigma}t^{maj(\sigma)}q^{\eta(\sigma)},$$ which are summed over all canonical or dual canonical fillings of a Young diagram, where $d_{\varepsilon}(\sigma)$ is a product of $q$-multinomials. Finally, the compact formulas enable us to derive four explicit expressions for the monomial expansion of modified Macdonald polynomials, one of which coincides with the formula due to Garbali and Wheeler (2020), obtained by making extensive use of the Yang-Baxter integrability approach.
item.dc:creator: Emma Yu Jin, Xiaowei Lin

item.title: Three-Neighbour Bootstrap Percolation in Thin Three-Dimensional Grids
item.description: arXiv:2509.13589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the status of the problem of determining minimum-sized percolating sets in $a \times b \times c$ grids under the $3$-neighbour process. Using several new constructions, we show that optimal percolating sets exist whenever $\min(a,b,c) \ge 7$. As an important step toward this, we also show that all grids with $\min(a,b,c) \ge 4$ have a percolating set whose size exactly achieves the lower bound $(ab+ac+bc)/3$ whenever this value is an integer.
item.dc:creator: Will Dolphin, Peter J. Dukes

item.title: Structure and Decomposition of Deltoids in Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2601.09774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deltoids provide a natural framework for studying defective (partial) matchings in abelian groups, and we develop both structure and existence results in this setting. Given finite subsets $A$ and $B$ of an abelian group $G$, a matching is a bijection $f:A\to B$ such that $af(a)\notin A$ for all $a\in A$, a definition motivated by the study of canonical forms for symmetric tensors. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a partial matching with any prescribed defect, and then describe the minimal unavoidable defect for a pair $(A,B)$. We also define and examine a defective version of Chowla sets in the matching context. We prove a structure theorem identifying obstructions to the existence of partial matchings with small defect. Finally, within the deltoid setup, we establish max-min results on the partitioning of $A$ and $B$ into left- and right-admissible sets. Our tools mix results from transversal theory with ideas from additive number theory.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Aliabadi, Jozsef Losonczy

item.title: An introduction to local differential privacy protocols using block designs
item.description: arXiv:2602.02744v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The design of protocols for local differential privacy (or LDP) has been a topic of considerable research interest in recent years. LDP protocols utilise the randomised encoding of outcomes of an experiment using a transition probability matrix (TPM). Several authors have observed that balanced incomplete block designs (BIBDs) provide nice examples of TPMs for LDP protocols. Indeed, it has been shown that such BIBD-based LDP protocols provide optimal estimators. In this primarily expository paper, we give a detailed introduction to LDP protocols and their connections with block designs. We prove that a subclass of LDP protocols known as pure LDP protocols are equivalent to $(r,\lambda)$-designs (which contain balanced incomplete block designs as a special case). An unbiased estimator for an LDP scheme is a left inverse of the transition probability matrix. We show that the optimal estimators for BIBD-based TPMs are precisely those obtained from the Moore-Penrose inverse of the corresponding TPM. We also review some existing work on optimal LDP protocols in the context of pure protocols.
item.dc:creator: Maura B. Paterson, Douglas R. Stinson

item.title: Path homology of circulant digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2602.04140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study GLMY path homology of circulant digraphs through step-word complexes and infinite cyclic lifts. We first prove chain retractions for interval connection sets. For a fixed finite positive connection set $S$ containing $1$, the infinite lift yields a split exact sequence and all-degree stability over every field. We then encode the short additive relations of $S$ in a lattice lift and obtain exterior homology in arbitrarily high degrees for collision-free step sets. Under an exact Freiman admissibility condition, we classify all connection sets with three positive steps. For arbitrarily many steps, we compute rectangular additive configurations and arithmetic progressions over every field, and doubling strings in characteristic zero, including their boundary ranks.
item.dc:creator: Xinxing Tang, Shing-Tung Yau

item.title: The Smallest String Attractors of Fibonacci, Period-Doubling, and Thue--Morse Words
item.description: arXiv:2602.16152v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A string attractor of a string $T[1..|T|]$ is a set of positions $\Gamma$ of $T$ such that any nonempty substring $w$ of $T$ has an occurrence that crosses a position in $\Gamma$, i.e., there is a position $i$ such that $w = T[i..i+|w|-1]$ and the intersection $[i,i+|w|-1]\cap \Gamma$ is nonempty. The size of the smallest string attractor of Fibonacci words and period-doubling words of length at least $2$ is known to be $2$. The size of the smallest string attractor of Thue--Morse words of length at least $25$ is known to be $4$. We completely characterize the set of all smallest string attractors of Fibonacci words, period-doubling words, and Thue--Morse words. For Fibonacci words, we show a recursive formula describing the $2^{n-4} + 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil - 2}$ distinct position pairs that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Fibonacci word for $n \geq 7$. For period-doubling words, we show a formula describing the two distinct position pairs that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th period-doubling word for $n\geq 2$. For Thue--Morse words, we show a formula describing the 32 sets of four positions that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Thue--Morse word for $n\geq 6$. Our results show that strings with the same smallest attractor size can have a drastically different number of distinct smallest attractors.
item.dc:creator: Mutsunori Banbara, Hideo Bannai, Peaker Guo, Dominik K\"oppl, Takuya Mieno, Yoshio Okamoto

item.title: Motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells and the connective formal group law
item.description: arXiv:2605.26556v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use the connective formal group law to define a one-parameter ($\beta$-)deformation of the motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells in the $d$-step flag variety. This $\beta$-deformation specializes to the motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells when $\beta=1$ and to the Segre-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of Schubert cells when $\beta=0$ (though the $\beta$-deformations are not simply the $\beta$-homogenizations of the motivic Segre classes). We define rational function representatives for the $\beta$-deformed classes in the $d=1$ case in terms of a solvable lattice model, and we prove a combinatorial formula for the structure constants in the $\beta$-deformed basis in the $d=1$ case using Knutson-Tao puzzles. Unexpectedly, the structure constants are built out of entries of $R$-matrices for the multi-parameter quantum group of type $\widehat{a}_2$ (which suggests an action of multi-parameter quantum groups on equivariant connective $K$-rings of Nakajima quiver varieties, with their convolution algebra structures). We show that our $\beta$-deformations arise from canonical elements in a quotient of the torus-equivariant algebraic cobordism ring of the cotangent bundle of the flag variety by proving that the canonical elements satisfy a GKM type condition (in future work, we will show that these canonical elements also lie in the torus-equivariant connective $K$-ring, in the sense of Karpenko--Merkurjev, of this cotangent bundle).
item.dc:creator: Raj Gandhi

item.title: Hitting Arithmetic Progressions at the Square-Root Scale
item.description: arXiv:2606.01780v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f(N,k)$ be the minimum size of a subset of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ meeting every $k$-term arithmetic progression of positive difference contained in that interval. Improving on a bound of Truss, we prove that \[ f(n^2,n)\ge n+n^{1-o(1)} \] as $n\to\infty$. Improving on a bound of Xu, for primes $p$ we prove that \[ f(p^2,p)\le2p-(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt{\frac p{\log p}}. \]
item.dc:creator: Samuel Korsky

item.title: Hamilton paths and cycles in flip graphs of (almost-)perfect matchings
item.description: arXiv:2607.04687v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the set of matchings of a graph and a local change operation, called a flip, between them. In the combinatorial setting, the base graphs are either complete graphs or complete bipartite graphs, and in the geometric setting, the graphs are embedded on point sets in the plane, with the requirement that edges must be drawn as straight lines and must not cross. For base graphs with an even number of vertices, we consider perfect matchings, i.e., all vertices are matched, and for base graphs with an odd number of vertices, we consider almost-perfect matchings, i.e., all but one vertex of the graph are matched. A 2-flip between two perfect matchings exchanges two edges, and a 1-flip between two almost-perfect matchings exchanges one edge. The corresponding flip graph has the set of perfect or almost-perfect matchings as vertices, with pairs of them connected by an edge if they differ in a 2-flip or 1-flip, respectively. In this work, we provide a comprehensive picture of Hamiltonicity properties of these flip graphs. We prove that the flip graphs in the combinatorial setting are Hamilton-connected, i.e., they admit a Hamilton path between any two vertices, or, if the flip graphs are bipartite, we prove that they are Hamilton-laceable, i.e., they admit a Hamilton path between any two vertices from different partition classes. In the geometric setting, we prove that any path in them misses exponentially many vertices, in particular, they have no Hamilton paths or cycles. For points in convex position and almost-perfect matchings under 1-flips, we complement this by constructing a cycle in the flip graph that visits almost all vertices.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Brenner, Justin Dallant, Linda Kleist, Robert Lauff, Torsten M\"utze, Torben Sch\"urenberg

item.title: A correction to the Zero Forcing Number of the Generalized Petersen Graphs $P(n,3)$
item.description: arXiv:2607.19412v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rashidi, Shajareh Poursalavati, and Tavakkoli [J. Algebra Comb. Discrete Struct. Appl. 7 (2020), no.2, 183-193, Theorem 3.6] claim $Z(P(n,3)) = 8$ for all $n \geq 12$, but this fails at $n = 12$, where $Z(P(12,3)) = 7$. We give an explicit $7$-vertex zero forcing set for $P(12,3)$ and its forcing sequence, and verify by exhaustive search that no $6$-vertex set forces $P(12,3)$. We prove $Z(P(n,3)) \le 8$ for $n \ge 9$ using an explicit forcing set and rotational symmetry. Exhaustive search yields $Z(P(n,3))$ for $7 \le n \le 20$ and identifies the gap in the published proof: its case analysis fails to exclude $7$-vertex sets. We conjecture $Z(P(n,3)) = 8$ for $n \ge 13$, requiring a matching lower bound for all large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Arnav Krishnan

item.title: Freeness of Arrangements with Regular Underlying Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2608.01331v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify freeness for finite central arrangements whose underlying matroids are regular. Let $\mathcal A$ be such an arrangement over an arbitrary field, and put $M=M(\mathcal A)$. Then $\mathcal A$ is free if and only if $M$ is supersolvable; equivalently, $M$ admits a nice partition; equivalently, $M$ is the cycle matroid of a chordal simple graph. Thus, for arrangements with regular underlying matroids, freeness has a complete combinatorial classification independent of the base field. We use Seymour's decomposition theorem for regular matroids to prove that freeness forces supersolvability. We also characterize nice partitions of finite simple binary matroids: a partition is nice if and only if it is independent and no line is contained in a single block. Consequently, a finite loopless binary matroid admits a nice partition if and only if it is simple and supersolvable.
item.dc:creator: Weikang Liang, Suijie Wang

item.title: A short proof of the Erd\H os--S\'os Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.15893v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Erd\H os--S\'os Conjecture was recently proved by GPT-6 Astra, using a very ingenious and surprising argument. In this note, we present a simplified version of this argument in an (arguably) more natural form. We also prove a related conjecture of Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares Sales, Reed and Thomass\'e, and give a substantially simplified proof of an analogous result for eulerian digraphs, again proved by GPT-6 Astra, and announced by Mubayi and Verstraete. In addition, we determine the extremal (di)graphs for all three problems.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Riordan, Alex Scott

item.title: Proof of Almkvist's conjecture on the unimodality of partition polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.23779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For integers $r\ge2$ and $n\ge1$, let $$ F_{r,n}(q)=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1-q^{rk}}{1-q^k}. $$ The coefficient of $q^j$ in \(F_{r,n}(q)\) counts partitions of $j$ into parts at most $n$, each occurring at most $r-1$ times. Hughes proved that $F_{2,n}(q)=\prod_{k=1}^{n}(1+q^k)$ is unimodal for every $n\ge 1$. This result was reproved by Stanley using an algebraic approach and Odlyzko and Richmond using an analytic approach. Almkvist conjectured that $F_{r,n}(q)$ is unimodal in the following two cases: every even $r$ and every $n\ge 1$; every odd $r$ and every $n\ge 11$. He proved that this conjecture is true for $3\le r \le 20$ and $r=100,101$. In this paper, we completely settle the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jianxi Mao, Wenle Shi, Bao-xuan Zhu

item.title: The stacking number of a tree
item.description: arXiv:2609.31811v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Csern\'ak and Soukup introduced the stacking number of a graph: the least integer $t\ge2$ such that every configuration of $t$ pebbles can be transformed by pebbling moves into a configuration supported on one vertex. They conjectured an explicit formula for the stacking number of a tree in terms of the degrees of its vertices and their distances from a chosen root. We prove this conjecture for every finite tree with at least two vertices. We also show that whether a configuration on a tree can be stacked at a given vertex is decided exactly by the sign of an integer score built from recursive branch messages; consequently, stackability can be tested with a linear number of arithmetic operations. The proof combines this criterion with an explicit zero-score obstruction and a weighted cancellation argument for arbitrary nonstackable configurations. The main theorem and the stackability criterion are formalized in Lean 4, and the main theorem has passed Palomar mechanical verification; it is publicly registered as PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000010.
item.dc:creator: John Fairfax-Ball

item.title: Counting hypergraphs without linear cycles of fixed length
item.description: arXiv:2609.38772v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $C_{k}^{(r)}$ be the $r$-uniform linear cycle on $k$ hyperedges. An $r$-graph is $C_{k}^{(r)}$-free if it contains no copy of $C_{k}^{(r)}$. Let $\operatorname{ex}_{r}(n,C_{k}^{(r)})$ denote the maximum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex $C_{k}^{(r)}$-free $r$-graph. Balogh, Narayanan and Skokan asked whether, for every pair of integers $r,k\ge 3$, the number of $C_k^{(r)}$-free $r$-graphs on $n$ labelled vertices is \[ 2^{(1+o(1))\operatorname{ex}_{r}(n,C_{k}^{(r)})}. \] While the analogous statement is known to fail for graphs ($r=2$), by a construction of Morris and Saxton, the general question remained open for hypergraphs. Very recently, Jiang and Longbrake answered the question affirmatively when $r\geq5$. In this paper, we completely resolve the problem by proving that the answer is affirmative for every pair of integers $r,k\geq3$. When $(r,k)\neq(3,3)$, we establish balanced supersaturation results for linear cycles and combine them with the hypergraph container method. For $(r,k)=(3,3)$, we instead decompose $3$-graphs according to their pair-codegrees, encode the subhypergraph formed by the hyperedges that contain a large codegree pair as a directed graph, and apply a multicolour entropy theorem.
item.dc:creator: J\'ozsef Balogh, Ramon I. Garcia, Abhishek Methuku

item.title: Covering Bridgeless Claw-Free Cubic Graphs with Perfect Matchings
item.description: arXiv:2610.01137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Berge conjecture [Proc. London Math. Soc., 1979] asserts that every bridgeless cubic graph can be covered by five perfect matchings. The 5-cycle double cover conjecture, proposed independently by Preissmann (1981) and Celmins (1984), asserts that every bridgeless graph admits five even subgraphs such that every edge belongs to exactly two of them. Hakobyan and Mkrtchyan [Ars Math. Contemp., 2019] proved that the 5-cycle double cover conjecture holds if and only if every bridgeless claw-free cubic graph can be covered by four perfect matchings. In this paper, we prove that the Berge conjecture holds for every bridgeless claw-free cubic graph $G$ and that $G$ has four perfect matchings covering at least $\frac{299}{315}|E(G)|$ edges.
item.dc:creator: Huaibin Zhou, Xiumei Wang

item.title: From Unit Interval Orders to Totally Nonnegative Matrices: Permanental Inequalities and Bruhat-Increasing Bijections
item.description: arXiv:2610.04809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an $n\times n$ matrix $A=(a_{i,j})$ and subsets $I,J$ of $[1,n]:=\{1,\dotsc,n\}$, let $A_{I,J}=(a_{i,j})_{i\in I,j\in J}$ denote the $(I,J)$-submatrix of $A$. We prove that, for every totally nonnegative matrix $A$ and every $h=1,\dotsc,n-1$, \begin{equation} \operatorname{perm}(A_{[1,h],[1,h]}) \operatorname{perm}(A_{[h+1,n],[h+1,n]}) \;\geq\; \operatorname{perm}(A_{[1,n]\cap 2\mathbb Z,[1,n]\cap 2\mathbb Z}) \operatorname{perm}(A_{[1,n]\smallsetminus 2\mathbb Z,[1,n]\smallsetminus 2\mathbb Z}). \label{eq:absmain} \end{equation} In particular, these inequalities hold for the $0$-$1$ totally nonnegative matrices arising as antiadjacency matrices of unit interval orders. Our proof is based on explicit Bruhat-order comparisons between two distinguished families of permutations. Let $\mathfrak{A}_n$ be the Young subgroup $\mathfrak{S}_{1,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor} \times \mathfrak{S}_{\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor+1,\ldots,n}$ and let $\mathfrak{B}_n$ be the set of parity-alternating permutations \begin{equation*} \{w=w_1\cdots w_n\in\mathfrak{S}_n \mid i \text{ and } w_i \text{ have the same parity}\}. \end{equation*} For the balanced case $h=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor$, we construct a bijection $f_n:\mathfrak{A}_n\rightarrow\mathfrak{B}_n$ satisfying $w\leq f_n(w)$ in Bruhat order. We then extend this construction to arbitrary $h$ by means of maps $g_{n,h}$ satisfying the corresponding Bruhat-order comparison. These maps yield the inequalities for all totally nonnegative matrices.
item.dc:creator: Sihong Pan, Mark Skandera, Jiayuan Wang

item.title: Descartes' rule of signs for arbitrary fewnomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.06435v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We give a multivariate generalization of this rule to arbitrary fewnomial systems: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes rules of signs for circuits of Bihan-Dickenstein and Bihan-Dickenstein-Forsg{\aa}rd. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii-Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a polyhedron $\Delta$. This polyhedron is a chamber of a hyperplane arrangement whose combinatorics is determined by the oriented matroid of the coefficient matrix. We bound the number of these zeros by the B\'ezout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving the signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends on lines with the Descartes rules for circuits. In this way the coefficients enter the bounds through the combinatorics of the arrangement, and the exponents through sign conditions on minors.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Projective dimension of closed neighborhood hypergraphs via extended double covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.06556v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite and simple graph without isolated vertices. We investigate the projective dimension of the closed neighborhood hypergraph $\mathcal{N}[G]$ and its relationship with the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the extended bipartite double cover $\mathfrak{B}_e(G)$ of $G$. We establish the general upper bound $\operatorname{prod-dim} (\mathcal{N}[G]) \leq \operatorname{reg}(\mathfrak{B}_e(G))$ for all graphs. Furthermore, we prove that the exact equalities $\operatorname{prod-dim} (\mathcal{N}[G]) = \operatorname{reg}(\mathfrak{B}_e(G)) =\alpha(G)$ hold when $G$ belongs to several prominent graph classes, including K\"onig-Egerv\'ary (contains all bipartite graphs), cographs, co-chordal, chordal and comparability graphs, where $\alpha(G)$ denotes the independence number. Our method of proofs relies on connecting algebraic invariants to the underlying combinatorial structure of graphs through covering, domination and matching parameters, together with the use of homology tools.
item.dc:creator: Yusuf Civan, Anurag Singh
